A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReMDM work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison; v3 additionally contains a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original ReMDM experiments on text generation, image generation, molecular guidance and downstream language tasks, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, parameter studies and generated examples.

M1.justification: The ReMDM posterior, training objective, remasking schedules, switch/loop procedures and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Renaming Section 3.1 and expanding explanations do not introduce a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpenWebText, ImageNet, QM9 ring-count and drug-likeness generation, Countdown and TruthfulQA. No dataset, domain or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines, including AR, SEDD, MDLM, FB, DFM, MaskGiT, UDLM and LLaDA variants where applicable. The added bibliography entries do not become evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same splits, models, sampling budgets, metrics and hyperparameter settings. The expanded Countdown description specifies arithmetic operations without reporting a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The component ablation, training-objective comparison, schedule sensitivity studies, generative-perplexity hacking analysis and molecular guidance analyses are retained. Appendices E–F contain the same analyses and examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 runs with seeds 0–19 and 95% confidence intervals for Table 3 in Appendix D.4. The new checklist explains the absence of error bars elsewhere but changes no uncertainty reporting practice or estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and the corresponding figures retain their results. For example, ReMDM's OpenWebText MAUVE at T=4096 remains 0.656, ImageNet FID at T=64 remains 4.45, and Countdown pass@1 remains 46.1 ± 0.2%.

T1.justification: The theorems, propositions, assumptions and derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B are unchanged. Numbering the NELBO and explaining an existing probability-decomposition step improve exposition without changing mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about remasking, pretrained-model reuse, inference-time scaling, sample quality, guidance and downstream performance.

C2.justification: Checklist item 7 newly explains that producing error bars for experiments outside Table 3 was considered too computationally expensive. Section 5.3 also removes the earlier qualification comparing its gains with Table 1; the principal interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.4 removes v2's estimate of about 30 minutes on one Nvidia A100 per downstream-task run. The new checklist adds conditional future code-release wording alongside the retained abstract's code link; this changes documentation without establishing an actual access change.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 63 to 69 references, adding works including Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes, Diffusion-LM and InfoDiffusion. Section 6's substantive positioning relative to DDIM and discrete corrector methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized explanatory edits in Sections 2–3 and Appendix A.4, renames Section 3.1, improves equation references, and adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The core organization and most main-text and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: All 31 figures and 10 tables are retained. Changes include an expanded Figure 4 caption, shortened Table 1 caption, more compact asset-table formatting and local page reflow, without new or redrawn plots.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through better probability-decomposition explanations, repaired NELBO equation references and a clearer Figure 4 caption. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of runtime information and less clear checklist wording about code release. The method and empirical support remain unchanged.
